### Prerequisites (listed separately)

1. `fixed_ext_surrender_value` -> `fixed_ext_surrender_part_year_interest`, form **state**. policy_source "The cash surrender value is not fixed until the contract carries the part-year interest credited for the surrender." — verbatim in `full_surrender_release` ("Fixing the value"), connective "not ... until" intact, hard gate, same-form restatement "Equivalently: while the contract does not yet carry that part-year interest credit, there is no fixed cash surrender value to tell the owner." Present in no other document (corpus search). Resolution basis: the depended-on doc `surrender_interest_credit` describes, in the sentence's words ("part-year ... interest", "credit"), the write: "the contract's interest is closed by crediting the part-year surrender interest, dated the day it is credited, to the contract value"; records: latest credit 2026-02-17, request received 2026-10-14, no later credit. Strength and connective match.
2. `fixed_ext_surrender_part_year_interest` -> `fixed_ext_missed_withdrawal_charge`, form **state**. policy_source "The part-year surrender interest is worked out only after every excess partial withdrawal on the contract carries its surrender charge entry." — verbatim in `surrender_interest_credit` ("Waiting state"), connective "only after" intact, same-form restatement "Put the other way: ...". In no other document. Resolution basis: `corrected_partial_withdrawal_charges`: "a withdrawal shown in the activity history as an excess partial withdrawal owes a surrender charge entry for partial withdrawal under the same withdrawal request. Where the activity history shows such a withdrawal and no such entry, the charge it owed ... is booked." Records: `excess_partial` 45000.00 under 7fc85467..., no `fixed_surrender_charge_assessed` row. Strength matches.
- The depended-on documents do not carry the blocked side's sentence; `condition`, `resolved_by` text appears nowhere as such (the depended-on hub describes its own write's effect in record terms, which is the resolution basis the skill requires).

## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the documents touched by this task was traced: hub rules, waiting states, tool blocks -> extended `rule`/`prerequisite.policy_source`/`task_tools.py`; computation docs -> `baseline.rule` (+ rule conventions); factor docs -> `factors[].ladder` and the rule sentences quoted in `compute_basis`; base provision docs -> base `policies[].rule` and `eligibility` (e.g. "The signatures relied on are those recorded on the surrender service request" <- `evidence_contract.authority: system_record`). Tier figures -> `variants[].parameters` (all six tiers checked: ladders, free pct/first year, renewal window, waiver ages, issue ages, premiums, declared rates, withholding 10%, deferral 180 days).

- Additions: none found. "The table states conditions without which no withdrawal is paid; it does not list everything a withdrawal is subject to" (`partial_withdrawal_provisions`) adds no obligation.
- Rewrites / omissions: none at entailment level.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call <tool>"): none — each task tool name occurs only in its own hub (checked over the corpus).
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none; every worked figure is labelled hypothetical and none reproduces this task's records (closest: SR7 rows in illustrative tables; values differ).

Policy-side notes (do not change this verdict):
- P1. `parameter_schema.free_withdrawal_pct` describes the parameter as the "share of the contract value on the most recent contract anniversary ... that may be withdrawn each contract year without surrender charge" — the semantics of the base clause the overwrites retire. The KB carries that description as the column note of `withdrawal_and_distribution_limits` ("The free withdrawal percentage is the share ..."), unmarked. It originates in the source (parameter schema not reconciled with the overwrite); it does not create a second solution because the computation and factor documents state the governing rule. Recorded, not re-judged.
- P2. The overwrites retire the base partial-withdrawal free-amount and charge clauses globally while the replacement sentences are scoped to corrected charges and full surrender; the source therefore states no in-force basis for the charge on an ordinary new partial withdrawal. The KB mirrors this faithfully (`partial_withdrawal_provisions` clauses 3 and 5 read with retired inserts). Policy-side.
- P3. The order sentence is carried by the source's own intermediate terms in the factor rules ("The capped ... percentage is reduced", "the reduced ... percentage is graded"); rendering them is faithful, see dependency_form.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** All atoms of the three extended policies (all 17 factor ladders tier by tier, both baselines' defaults and assemblies, both prerequisite sentences, all three tool contracts), the governing base clauses and the retired surface correspond at entailment level. Affected documents: none. First revision.

## dependency_form

- Prerequisite sentences: each stands verbatim, once, in its blocked policy's hub with only same-form restatements; neither is restated as an action, neither names a performer, tool or other problem.
- Other problems' tool names: none outside their own hubs.
- Routes / aggregated chains / dependency tables / ordered cross-problem step lists: none in any of the 65 documents.
- Wrong-vs-right contrasts or examples walking across problems: none; basis questions and worked cases stay inside one policy.
- Titles/openings: general subjects ("Release of a Full Surrender" is the on_request subject; "Closing Interest Credit on a Full Surrender"; "Corrected Partial-Withdrawal Surrender Charges"; factor titles name the rule, not a customer situation).
- Findability of depended-on docs: reachable through the record and sentence words ("part-year surrender interest", "excess partial withdrawal", "surrender charge entry").
- Factor docs: none states which tier customers fall on, none writes task evidence as fact. Cross-factor terms "capped percentage"/"reduced percentage" in the whole life and grading docs are the source rule's own wording fixing the order (overwrite `replaced_by` and rule), not a pointer added by the rendering — policy-side note, not RED.
- Computation docs: no "unless otherwise provided", "adjustments may apply", exception list or pointer. Observation only: `partial_withdrawal_charge_computation` and `cash_surrender_value_computation` close with the rule's convention line "ages are whole years last birthday from the annuitant's date of birth", which their own formulas do not use; the line comes from the source `rule`, states a convention rather than a modification, and is not a hint in the sense of the scan.

**PASS** (KB-EXPLICIT).
